newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq's ruling party elects new senior members.
newsitem.headline: Iraq's ruling party elects new senior members.

text.p: Iraq's ruling Baath party has elected two senior members to its regional command, the official Iraqi news agency INA reported on Tuesday.
The new members are Latif Nsayyif Jassim, a former information minister who is currently Minister of Labour and Social Affairs and Adel Abdullah Mehdi, a senior member of the party's Baghdad branch.
The Baath party's regional command is the highest authority in Iraq after the ruling Revolutionary Command Council.

The agency, reporting the ballot during the party's annual congress held on Monday and chaired by President Saddam Hussein, said Jassim and Mehdi were elected from 11 Baathists nominated for the two seats on the 16-member regional command. The elections were held by 267 party members who attended the congress.
"In the light of the party's need for additional members to carry out the command's duties in the next stage...the leadership (of the party) proposed the election of two new members," INA said.
Saddam is the party's secretary-general. Veteran politician Izzat Ibrahim is the party deputy leader and vice-chairman of the Revolutionary Command Council.

Among the members of the party's command are Deputy Premier Tareq Aziz, former prime minister Mohammed Hamza al-Zubeidi, former defence minister Ali Hassan al-Majeed and former information minister Abd-al-Ghani Abd-al-Ghafur.
Abd-al-Ghafur was relieved of his ministerial post on Thursday and replaced by Hamed Youssef Hummadi.
